Article Title: Small island states can serve as labs for innovation and tech: Maldives prez
Article Text:
Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu also announced plans for the country's first Trade Acceleration Zone.

Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu called upon Small Island Developing States (SIDS) to pivot away from being framed solely by climate vulnerability and isolation, while also urging global leaders and private sector partners to view island economies as dynamic "laboratories for innovation".Delivering a keynote statement at the opening ceremony of the Small Island Developing States Global Business Network (SIDS GBN) Forum 2026, Muizzu outlined an economic modernization plan aimed at turning geographic constraints into digital and strategic advantages.With the global dialogue surrounding small island nations focused on their acute climate risk, geographical isolation, and structural economic constraints, Muizzu stressed that vulnerability represents only half the story."For too long, the story of Small Island Developing States has been told primarily through the lens of vulnerability. The other part is our determination. Our scale can become an advantage. SIDS can serve as laboratories for innovation and incubators for ideas, technologies, and solutions,” he said.The president's address focused on the Maldives 2.0 agenda, designed to leverage technology to overcome the traditional barriers of an archipelagic state.Under this strategic initiative, the Maldivian government aims to expand its digital and creative sectors, setting a target for these industries to account for 15 percent of national GDP by 2030.“We have identified the digital economy and digitalisation as central to advancing our economy. Through our Maldives 2.0 agenda, we are working to use digital connectivity to overcome the limitations of geography and scale — making government and financial services more accessible, enabling businesses to operate more efficiently, and connecting Maldivian enterprises and talent to global markets,” said Muizzu.The Maldives is enhancing financial technology accessibility for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs). Key measures include launching homegrown digital payment platforms such as BML Swipe and expanding international gateway integration through services like PayPal.Muizzu also announced plans for the country's first Trade Acceleration Zone, set to launch by January 1, 2027, to incentivize enterprise development and fast-track commercial growth.While reaffirming the Maldives' commitment to attracting international capital through a modernized foreign investment framework, Muizzu stressed that foreign partnerships must align with national interests. New legal safeguards have been introduced to protect domestic commerce by reserving specific commercial activities strictly for local entities, ensuring economic growth directly benefits Maldivian citizens, he stressed.Muizzu called upon international investors, technology companies, and global financial institutions to establish concrete commercial partnerships with small island states. He reiterated the Maldives' commitment to implementing the Antigua and Barbuda Agenda for SIDS (ABAS), urging global stakeholders to bridge the gap between initial innovation and sustainable commercial financing.
Article Summary: Maldives president mohamed muizzu called upon small island developing states (sids) to pivot away from being framed solely by climate vulnerability and isolation. He urged global leaders and private sector partners to view island economies as dynamic "laboratories for innovation" muizzu outlined an economic modernization plan aimed at turning geographic constraints into digital and strategic advantages.

Article Title: "E20 fuel hazardous for pre-2023 vehicles, auto firms silenced by fear of raids": Arvind Kejriwal
Article Text:
"E20 fuel hazardous for pre-2023 vehicles, auto firms silenced by fear of raids": Arvind Kejriwal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

AAP National Convenor Arvind Kejriwal on Tuesday stepped up his attack on the Centre's nationwide rollout of E20 petrol, alleging that auto majors are being forced to stay silent on its risks.Addressing a press conference in Goa ahead of a town hall on the issue, Kejriwal claimed top officials of leading car and bike companies have privately admitted that E20 fuel can cause severe damage to vehicles manufactured before 2023, but are refusing to speak publicly due to government pressure.Kejriwal said he wrote letters to 29 automobile manufacturing companies, asking them whether E20 fuel could be safely used in vehicles manufactured by them before 2023. He said he received no response to the letters."I wrote letters to 29 auto manufacturing companies. I asked them whether E20 fuel could be safely used in vehicles they had manufactured prior to 2023. I received no response," Kejriwal said.He said he subsequently spoke to officials from nine automobile companies, who, according to him, spoke candidly about the issue but requested that their identities and the names of their companies not be disclosed.According to Kejriwal, the officials told him that E20 is a "very dangerous fuel" and that using it in petrol-based vehicles manufactured before 2023 would be "extremely hazardous" for those vehicles.However, he claimed that the officials were unwilling to speak publicly about the issue because they were under pressure from the Central Government."They stated that E20 is a very dangerous fuel and using it in petrol-based vehicles manufactured before 2023 would be extremely hazardous for the vehicles," Kejriwal said.He further alleged that the automobile company officials feared that speaking against E20 could result in action by central investigative and tax agencies."However, they said they could not speak out publicly because they are under immense pressure from the Central Government, and speaking against E20 could trigger raids by the ED, CBI, or Income Tax Department against them, or even lead to the closure of their plants," he said.Kejriwal also claimed that the officials were being "harassed in various ways" and therefore did not want their identities or company names to be made public.His remarks came in the context of concerns over the use of E20 fuel in petrol vehicles manufactured before 2023.The AAP leader did not disclose the names of the companies or the officials he said he had spoken to.Opposing the Centre's forced rollout of E20 fuel (20% ethanol, 80% petrol), the Aam Aadmi Party said the blend has triggered complaints of reduced mileage, engine damage and early wear of fuel components, with pre-2023 vehicles being the worst hit.Kejriwal's remarks come as part of AAP's series of town halls across major states. The party has been demanding that the Central Government reinstate consumer choice at petrol pumps by offering standard petrol alongside ethanol blends.
Article Summary: "e20 fuel hazardous for pre-2023 vehicles, auto firms silenced by fear of raids": arvind kejriwal. "i wrote letters to 29 auto manufacturing companies. I asked them whether e20 fuel could be safely used in vehicles they had manufactured prior to 2023," he said.

Article Title: EU approvals, easier sterilisation rules to speed device access
Article Text:
Faster access to some newer medical devices. (Representative image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Patients in India could get faster access to some newer medical devices already approved in the European Union, with the government expanding its list of trusted foreign regulatory jurisdictions while also easing licensing requirements for manufacturers outsourcing sterilisation.The Health Ministry has amended the Medical Devices Rules, 2017 to include the European Union among jurisdictions recognised for waiver of clinical investigation requirements for eligible medical devices that do not have a predicate device in India. The list earlier included the US, UK, Australia, Canada and Japan.The change means eligible devices that have already received regulatory approval in the EU can potentially avoid a fresh clinical investigation in India, reducing the time and regulatory steps required before they can be made available to patients. The waiver remains subject to the conditions prescribed under the rules.The government said the move would reduce regulatory timelines for manufacturers and importers and facilitate faster availability of advanced medical technologies in India. The addition of the EU also brings India’s medical-device regulatory framework closer to international regulatory practices.Separately, manufacturers outsourcing sterilisation to a facility with a valid licence will no longer need a separate loan licence, reducing paperwork, compliance costs and delays.However, they will still have to print the sterilisation facility’s licence number on the device label, with six months to comply. The labelling requirement had drawn industry concerns over added compliance burden and possible export delays.The government has also introduced a standard fee schedule for testing and evaluation of medical devices. The new charges include Rs 5,000 for implantation tests, Rs 2,000 for sterility testing, Rs 1,000 for syringes and needles and Rs 3,000 for surgical sutures. Testing fees for condoms and intrauterine devices have been fixed at Rs 2,500 each.For tests not specified in the schedule, the charges will be decided by the concerned laboratory or medical device testing officer. The prescribed fees will automatically rise by 5% annually.The three changes are aimed at cutting regulatory duplication, making compliance costs more predictable and speeding up access to medical devices while retaining requirements for quality, safety and traceability. The sterilisation and testing-fee amendments were notified as the Medical Devices (Second Amendment) Rules, 2026.
Article Summary: The health ministry has amended the medical devices rules, 2017 to include the european union among jurisdictions recognised for waiver of clinical investigation requirements. The list earlier included the us, uk, australia, canada and japan.

Article Title: ‘100%’, ‘Energy Drink’, immunity claims: FSSAI flags 6 food firms
Article Text:
FSSAI flagged 6 food companies for misleading claims on products like coconut oil, energy drinks, and baby food.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Claims that promise more, sound healthier or make a product appear superior have come under the scanner of the food regulator, with the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) flagging misleading claims by six food business operators (FBOs) and directing corrective action.The cases range from the use of “100%” on coconut oil and “Energy Drink” on a caffeinated beverage to claims around immunity, growth, digestion and nutrition in baby food, as well as health and nutrient-comparison claims.Mondelez India Foods Pvt Ltd was flagged over misleading health and nutrient comparative claims. It subsequently withdrew the claims and advertisements from e-commerce platforms.Sapiens Labs was flagged over a misleading claim and, after submitting its response, withdrew the claim and advertisements.Vichi Agro Products Pvt Ltd, along with the concerned packer, was flagged over a misleading trade name and deleted the product from its platform.In a separate case, Amway India Enterprises Pvt Ltd, Delhi, was flagged over the use of “100%” in the name “100% Pure Coconut Oil”. The company said it had voluntarily removed the term from packaging and promotional material and discontinued old stock from sales channels.Revised packaging without the claim has been finalised and is being rolled out progressively from September-October 2026.In Kerala, Juza Foods, Malappuram, was flagged over multiple claims for its baby food products, including claims relating to nutrition, immunity, growth, digestion and nutrient content, besides comparisons with other milk powders. The company acknowledged the violations and agreed to remove the misleading claims.It also said its selling website had been shut and rectification completed, while steps were being taken for licence-related changes and an e-commerce licence.Amway India was also flagged separately over use of the term “Energy Drink” on a caffeinated beverage. The company accepted the observation and removed the term from its product range, website and promotional material. Updated packaging is to be introduced from the production cycle beginning August 2026.The cases highlight the kinds of claims and product descriptions that can come under FSSAI scrutiny, particularly when they could influence how consumers perceive a food product.
Article Summary: Fssai flagged 6 food companies for misleading claims on products like coconut oil, energy drinks, and baby food. Claims that promise more, sound healthier or make a product appear superior have come under the scanner of the food regulator. The cases range from the use of “100%” on coconut oil and “energy drink’ on a caffeinated beverage.

Article Title: FSSAI crackdown: Food companies withdraw ‘100%’ and health claims after notices
Article Text:
FSSAI's crackdown on misleading claims (representative image)

Amway removes 'Energy Drink' and '100%' claims

Juza Foods agrees to remove baby food claims

Products delisted, advertisements withdrawn

Action comes amid wider FSSAI enforcement drive

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) on Tuesday said several major food business operators (FBOs) had taken corrective action following notices issued over misleading labels, claims and other regulatory violations.In a post on X, the food regulator said the measures included withdrawal of misleading label claims and changes to product packaging to ensure consumer safety and regulatory compliance.Among the companies named by FSSAI were Amway India Enterprises, Juza Foods, Mondelez India Foods and Sapiens Labs, while another case involved a product marketed by Vichi Agro Products and processed and packed by J J Foods.FSSAI said Amway India Enterprises Pvt Ltd had accepted its directions and removed the term "Energy Drink" from its XS product range.According to the regulator, the product was a caffeinated beverage licensed under food category 14.1, but carried the term "Energy Drink". Amway confirmed that it had removed the word "Energy" from its product artwork, website and promotional materials.FSSAI said Amway had clarified that the descriptor was originally adopted in good faith following an FSSAI advisory issued in March 2024. The company said revised packaging would take effect from the next production cycle in August 2026.Amway also requested permission to sell existing stock carrying the earlier artwork until the inventory was exhausted in the ordinary course of trade, while the revised packaging is introduced.In a separate case, FSSAI said Amway had also removed the term "100%" from its product name "100% Pure Coconut Oil", citing violations related to food labelling and advertising claims.The company submitted a compliance response confirming that it had removed the claim from its packaging and promotional material and discontinued old stock from sales channels.Revised packaging has been finalised and is in production, with the new packaging expected to be rolled out progressively from September-October 2026, along with updated website listings.FSSAI also highlighted action taken by Juza Foods, Malappuram, Kerala, over multiple claims made for its baby food products.The regulator listed claims including "pure", "natural", "traditional", "no artificial colours, flavours or preservatives" and "Your baby's 1st taste of Real Nutrition".It also flagged health claims such as products being "ideal for sensitive babies", "easy to digest", offering "better absorption", and helping to "boost immunity" and "support stronger bones".FSSAI also cited claims including "100% Ragi", "100% vegan", "100% Kerala Banana powder" and "100% sweet potato powder", along with comparative claims that the products contained "10X the calcium of wheat and rice" and "3X the calcium of Milk".The regulator further said the company had been conducting its food business through an online website without having e-commerce listed as a Kind of Business in its licence.Juza Foods acknowledged the violations and agreed to remove the misleading claims, FSSAI said. Its selling website has been shut down until the rectification is completed, while the company has applied for modification of its licence and for an e-commerce category.In another case, FSSAI said a product marketed by Vichi Agro Products Pvt Ltd and processed and packed by J J Foods was flagged over a misleading trade name.A response received from Flipkart stated that the food business operator had delisted the product from the platform.FSSAI also said Mondelez India Foods Pvt Ltd had withdrawn claims and advertisements from e-commerce platforms following action over misleading health claims and nutrient comparative claims.Sapiens Labs similarly submitted a response and withdrew all claims and advertisements after FSSAI flagged a misleading claim on its own initiative.The latest update comes amid a broader FSSAI enforcement drive against misleading advertisements, false claims and labelling violations.The regulator said recently that it had issued more than 150 notices to food companies, including Nestle India, PepsiCo, Abbott India, Red Bull India, Danone India, Monster Energy India, Hell Energy, Mondelez India, Coca-Cola India, Diageo, Pernod Ricard, Ferrero India and Kenvue.FSSAI has also issued notices to e-commerce companies and food service establishments over alleged regulatory violations..The regulator has separately been taking action against the use of "100%" claims on food labels and advertisements. In an earlier update, FSSAI said several companies, including Amway India, Emami, Bonn Biscuits, Apis India, Juza Foods and Masterchow Foods, had taken corrective measures after being asked to discontinue such claims.
Article Summary: Fssai said several major food business operators (fbos) had taken corrective action following notices issued over misleading labels, claims and other regulatory violations. Among the companies named by fssai were amway india enterprises, juza foods, mondelez india foods and sapiens labs.

Article Title: Prevent misuse of data by private entities, SC tells government
Article Text:
SC flags private access to sensitive PF, I-T data, asks Centre to prevent misuse by firms

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday expressed concern about a commercial technological ecosystem which allegedly accesses, retrieves and verifies sensitive individual information on provident fund and income tax returns and told the Centre about the desirability of devising an antidote to the problem with the assistance of domain experts.Hearing a PIL by Piyush Sharma, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana noted the matter essentially fell within policy domain but termed private access to sovereign data - individual information given to govt under legislative mandate - and its commercial exploitation as worrisome.Petitioner said his personal inquiry into the issue had revealed that "upon merely furnishing PAN and UAN details to a private verification workflow, the petitioner received complete employment history corresponding the said identifiers. No OTP authentication was generated. No explicit consent was obtained. No visible authorisation-based identity verification process was undertaken".Without blaming govt agencies for any leakage of data, the petitioner highlighted the insecure status of individual data given to govt under the mandate of different laws, as they are accessed at will by private entities."Despite the statutory architecture governing EPFO and I-T data, there appears to be an emerging and concerning pattern wherein private employment verification ecosystems rely upon data corresponding to statutory employment and financial records for purposes such as employment verification, moonlighting detection, dual employment screening, labour market profiling and employment decision-making," he said.SC agreed it was a serious matter but said it must be dealt with through a policy decision. On learning the petitioner sent two comprehensive representations on the issues to Centre, it asked govt to take "necessary steps to prevent misuse of individual data by private enterprises."
Article Summary: Sc flags private access to sensitive pf, i-t data, asks centre to prevent misuse by firms. Petitioner said his personal inquiry into the issue had revealed that "upon merely furnishing pan and uan details to a private verification workflow, the petitioner received complete employment history corresponding the said identifiers"

Gisele Bündchen and Tom Brady built one of the most powerful celebrity fortunes of their generation, but their paths to wealth were very different. Bündchen is widely estimated to be worth around, while Brady’s current fortune is estimated by some sources at roughly. The surprising part is not that Brady became enormously wealthy. It is how consistently Bündchen’s fashion career generated money on a global scale.Gisele Bündchen entered modeling as a teenager and turned a traditional fashion career into a worldwide business. She became the world’s highest-paid model for much of the period from 2002 through 2017, according to Forbes-linked reporting.Her earnings did not depend on runway appearances alone. Major campaigns, beauty contracts, fragrances and brand partnerships helped transform her fame into long-term income. Forbes reported that Bündchen earned about $30.5 million in 2016, with deals involving brands such as Chanel and Carolina Herrera, alongside her own business ventures.Her career earnings were remarkable even before she stepped away from regular runway work. Forbes estimated in 2014 that she had earned $386 million from modeling since 2001.That helps explain the wealth gap. Bündchen was not simply being paid to wear clothes.She became the face of international brands and developed businesses connected to her name.Her income also continued beyond modeling through products, endorsements and investments. That broader strategy allowed her to turn a highly visible career into lasting wealth.Brady’s fortune was built differently. His biggest financial engine was his 23-year NFL career, during which he collected substantial playing salaries and bonuses. Forbes reported that he earned about $333 million from playing contracts, with another $200 million coming from endorsements and other ventures.But Brady has never relied solely on football. His business portfolio includes the TB12 brand, the BRADY clothing line, production ventures and Autograph. He has also invested in professional sports teams, including the Las Vegas Raiders and other franchises.His post-NFL career added another major income stream. Brady signed a reportedto become its lead NFL analyst.So, how is Gisele Bündchen richer than Tom Brady?The answer is timing, scale and the economics of their industries. Bündchen reached the top of a global fashion market for years, earning enormous endorsement income while building businesses of her own. Brady earned extraordinary sums from football, but his biggest playing contracts arrived within a sport where even the greatest players had different salary structures.Their fortunes also show why celebrity wealth cannot be judged simply by fame. Brady may have seven Super Bowl rings, but Bündchen built a global commercial brand that kept generating value far beyond the runway.

Burnham's government overhaul

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has appointed Indian-origin strategist and former BBC executive Gautam Rangarajan as an Expert Adviser on Structure and Process in a newly created role at 10 Downing Street.Rangarajan, who brings decades of experience in strategy, organisational transformation and media, is set to take up the position this week.Rangarajan is a senior strategist and media executive with more than two decades of experience across media, creative industries and public service broadcasting.Before his new government role, he spent more than 30 years at the BBC, beginning his career as a radio music producer and eventually rising to become the broadcaster's Group Director for Strategy and Performance.His experience includes developing strategy in rapidly changing markets, leading large-scale transformation initiatives and handling complex policy and financial negotiations.The exact details of Rangarajan's responsibilities are yet to be outlined. Article Title: Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox: "I think the scariest person in the world is the person with…" - a lesson on humour, perspective and facing hard times with lightness
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox (AP photo)

Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox

"I think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor"

Where this quote actually comes from

Why humour matters most during genuinely difficult stretches

How humour actually helps people manage stress

Why laughing at your own mistakes actually matters

Why humour can genuinely strengthen relationships

Michael J. Fox's own perspective on adversity

Why humour is not the same thing as avoiding a real problem

Why being naturally serious is not actually a flaw

Other memorable quotes by Michael J. Fox

"One's dignity may be assaulted, vandalized and cruelly mocked, but it can never be taken away unless it is surrendered."

"I am careful not to confuse excellence with perfection."

"Family is not an important thing. It's everything."

"Acceptance doesn't mean resignation; it means understanding that something is what it is and that there's got to be a way through it."

Why people still find meaning in this quote

Humour can genuinely change how a difficult moment actually feels. A stressful situation seems lighter once someone finds a reason to laugh, and a serious problem often becomes easier to approach once it can be seen from another angle. It can create a little distance from fear, frustration and uncertainty, even when the circumstances themselves have not changed. Michael J. Fox , the actor and Parkinson's disease advocate, put a striking twist on that idea. "I think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor," he said. Not being able to laugh, in his framing, is not simply a personality quirk. It genuinely limits how someone can respond to life, and coming from someone who has lived with a serious, lifelong illness for decades, the line carries a good deal more weight than a passing joke.This line comes from an interview Fox gave to journalist Amy Wallace, published on Reader's Digest's website. Fox is not really suggesting that a humourless person is dangerous in any literal sense. He is pointing at the seriousness that tends to surround someone who cannot laugh at themselves, cannot recognise irony, and cannot find any lightness in a genuinely difficult moment. Humour creates real distance from a problem.It lets someone acknowledge that something is hard without letting it completely take over.Life inevitably brings disappointment, uncertainty and real stress. Humour cannot solve every problem on its own, but it can genuinely change how someone responds to one. Being able to laugh during a hard period offers a small emotional break, and it can help people communicate when a direct, serious conversation feels too uncomfortable to actually have. None of this means every situation deserves to be treated as a joke. Humour and genuine seriousness can exist side by side.Stress tends to narrow someone's attention down entirely onto the immediate problem in front of them. A moment of real laughter can interrupt that cycle. Research into humour and stress has suggested that positive humour can genuinely influence mood and help people cope with stressful experiences, and laughter itself is linked to physiological changes, including a release of muscle tension. None of this should be overstated. Humour is never a substitute for professional help or a practical solution when someone faces a genuinely serious problem. As an everyday coping tool, though, it can offer a genuinely useful shift in perspective.One of the most valuable forms of humour is simply being able to laugh at your own missteps. Nobody gets everything right. People mispronounce words, misjudge situations and occasionally embarrass themselves, and someone who can acknowledge a mistake without being consumed by embarrassment tends to find it easier to actually learn from it. Self-directed humour also tends to make social interactions considerably more comfortable, since it signals that a person does not expect flawless perfection from either themselves or anyone else around them.Shared laughter helps people form real connections. Friends, colleagues and family members often use humour to build a sense of familiarity and trust, and a well-placed joke can break tension that a serious conversation might struggle to shift on its own. There is an important line here worth being clear about, between humour that actually brings people together and humour that humiliates someone else. Jokes built on cruelty or prejudice tend to damage relationships rather than genuinely strengthen them, and the most constructive kind of humour has never really needed anyone else to get hurt.Fox became one of the most recognisable actors of his generation through films and television, including Back to the Future and Family Ties. In 1991, at the age of 29, he was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. He later made the diagnosis public and became a prominent advocate for Parkinson's research through the Michael J. Fox Foundation. His public approach to living with the condition has consistently included honesty, genuine optimism and humour, which gives his comments about laughter an extra dimension. His point was never that difficult experiences are inherently funny. It is that holding onto a sense of humour can help someone preserve real perspective while actually facing a genuine challenge. His decades-long relationship with humour, cultivated alongside a chronic illness he never chose, reveals that laughter was never a denial of hardship for Fox, but a deliberate, hard-won tool for maintaining perspective and genuine hope through real adversity.There is a meaningful difference between using humour to cope with something difficult and using it to avoid actually dealing with it at all. Some problems genuinely require serious attention and real action, and nobody can simply laugh away financial difficulty, illness or grief. What humour can offer instead is a small amount of emotional breathing space while someone continues addressing the actual underlying issue, which is really the whole distinction worth holding onto here.Fox's quote is deliberately provocative, and it should not be read as suggesting that serious people are inherently unpleasant. Some people naturally have quieter personalities, or simply express humour in a different way. The broader lesson is really about flexibility rather than personality type. Someone who can be genuinely serious when it matters, while still finding moments of humour elsewhere, tends to have more ways of responding to life's challenges than someone who treats every single situation with exactly the same level of weight.Humour is easy to underrate, since it can look insignificant next to more obviously serious qualities like intelligence or discipline. Even so, the ability to laugh genuinely shapes how people communicate, handle their own mistakes and respond to real difficulty. Fox's quote offers a deliberately provocative reminder that life does not always need to be approached with complete seriousness. There will be moments when humour is genuinely inappropriate, and problems that cannot be laughed away at all. In between those moments, though, holding onto a sense of humour tends to keep people connected, flexible and hopeful, which is really the whole point behind the line.
Article Summary: "i think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor" michael j. Fox, actor and parkinson's disease advocate. Not being able to laugh is not simply a personality quirk. It genuinely limits how someone can respond to life. Michael j. Fox was one of the most recognisable actors of his generation.

Article Title: At Claude-maker Anthropic, candidates cannot negotiate on salary; as company follows standard process for compensation where what you are offered is…
Article Text:
Pages from the Anthropic website and the company's logo are displayed on a computer screen in New York on Thursday, Feb. 26, 2026. (AP Photo/Patrick Sison)

What happens in an Anthropic culture interview , according to candidates

Why Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is worried about who is walking through the door

At Anthropic, the AI lab behind Claude, the number on your offer letter is the number you sign. There is no back and forth, no counteroffer, no polite haggling over equity. Axios reports the company runs a standard process for both interviews and compensation, and negotiation simply is not part of it. For an industry where researchers are reportedly commanding eight-figure packages and switching labs every few months, that is an unusual position to take.The no-negotiation policy also sits next to something stranger. Every Anthropic candidate goes through a culture interview, conducted by an employee nominated for the task, and Axios reports it now includes a question built to test whether you would choose the mission over your own payday. One applicant, who spoke anonymously for fear of hurting future job prospects, recalled being asked how they would feel if Anthropic abandoned its AI ambitions for safety reasons and the stock went to zero.According to a former Anthropic employee familiar with the process, these questions are suggested rather than fully scripted. That would explain why applicants remember them differently. Some recall a literal stock crash scenario, others a broader conversation about safety trade-offs that could hurt revenue.Candidates are also asked to describe a moral quandary they have faced and how they dealt with it.One writer on the anonymous workplace forum Blind said they answered truthfully, admitting they would not be thrilled about a wipeout, and added that they would want to align doing the most good and remaining ethical while building a sustaining business. The interviewer, by their account, was not impressed.The context here matters. Axios previously reported that CEO Dario Amodei has expressed concern that newer hires are coming to Anthropic for the money rather than the mission, a remark that got heavily mocked online given the company reportedly pays at or near the top of the AI market. The talent churn is real, though. Lilian Weng became the fourth Thinking Machines co-founder to exit in a year before resurfacing at OpenAI, while Google lost Noam Shazeer to OpenAI and Nobel winner John Jumper to Anthropic in June.Two former Anthropic employees told Axios the stock-to-zero question was not always part of the process, and Blind posts suggest it started appearing in 2025. Co-founder and president Daniela Amodei, in a Bain Capital video from two years ago, said the culture interview has existed since day one.None of this is putting people off. Axios notes, citing Bloomberg, that candidates are spending thousands of dollars on private coaching and mock interviews with engineers from rival labs. Interviewing.io founder Aline Lerner framed the maths bluntly: a few thousand spent now against a salary bump of $200,000.Anthropic has form on the money-versus-mission trade-off. It walked away from a US military deal that would have granted unfettered government use of its technology, and it restricted access to Mythos, its most cyber-capable model. The company's careers page uses the word "mission" six times. Salary may be non-negotiable at Anthropic, but conviction, apparently, still has to be argued for.
Article Summary: Anthropic runs a standard process for both interviews and compensation, and negotiation simply is not part of it. Ceo dario amodei has expressed concern that newer hires are coming to anthropic for the money rather than the mission. Candidates are spending thousands of dollars on private coaching and mock interviews.

Article Title: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu shares why giving employees more freedom can feel ‘chaotic’; says ‘There is always …’
Article Text:
Sridhar Vembu on why freedom can feel ‘chaotic’

Sridhar Vembu: 'Every smart programmer’ thinks they can do better

Here’s the post shared by Sridhar Vembu

Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has shared his views on a workplace question many companies face: Should employees wait for instructions from their leaders or take the initiative and act on their own? In a post on X (formerly known as Twitter), Sridhar Vembu said giving people more freedom to take initiative can create an energetic but sometimes chaotic work culture. Employees may disagree strongly with one another and constantly feel that things can be improved. “There is always the gnawing feeling of ‘not good enough’,” Vembu wrote, explaining the trade-off between certainty and initiative in an organisation.In the post, Sridhar Vembu said highly metric-driven organisations often create a culture where employees wait for instructions from the top. Such workplaces can offer more predictability and certainty.However, he warned that this approach has its risks. “Unless the top always knows how to set the right course, the org can be lost,” Vembu wrote.On the other hand, an organisation where people are encouraged to take initiative can be less predictable. Employees with energy and strong ideas may disagree with each other, he said.“Seize the initiative culture” often feels chaotic, with lots of internal disagreements.There is always the gnawing feeling of “not good enough”,” Vembu wrote.The Zoho founder also used programmers as an example to explain why initiative-driven workplaces can see frequent disagreements.“People who are full of energy and initiative often vehemently disagree with other,” he wrote, adding: “I joke about this: every smart programmer looks at another programmer's code and thinks ‘it sucks, I can do better’!”According to Vembu, this is the trade-off companies need to understand when building their culture. A workplace can provide employees with comfortable certainty but risk losing their initiative. Alternatively, it can encourage people to take initiative while accepting the discomfort and disagreements that may come with it."On org culture: Do people wait for instructions from the top? Or do they seize the initiative and run?Highly metric driven orgs tend to produce the "wait for instructions from the top" culture and there is more predictability and certainty in that culture. Unless the top always knows how to set the right course, the org can be lost."Seize the initiative culture" often feels chaotic, with lots of internal disagreements. There is always the gnawing feeling of "not good enough". In a chaotic initiative-driven culture, the external environment (market) may have to provide the occasional discipline.People who are full of energy and initiative often vehemently disagree with other. I joke about this: every smart programmer looks at another programmer's code and thinks "it sucks, I can do better"!That is your trade-off in org cultures. We can provide comfortable certainty but lose the initiative or we can seize the initiative but keep feeling somewhat uncomfortable.In my experience, trying to square this circle: "we will have a highly disciplined culture of seizing the initiative" produces the worst of both worlds."
Article Summary: Sridhar vembu: giving people more freedom to take initiative can create an energetic but sometimes chaotic work culture. “seize the initiative culture” often feels chaotic, with lots of internal disagreements. There is always the gnawing feeling of ‘not good enough’,” he wrote.

Article Title: Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta and Nvidia; Sam Altman is 'worried' about you; as may be one day ...
Article Text:
Sam Altman cautioned that fears of AI breaking free from human oversight

Sam Altman admits he was ‘very wrong’ on OpenAI’s AI timeline after GPT-4

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says he worries that artificial intelligence could one day be controlled by only a handful of companies, models or individuals, leaving most consumers without influence over how the technology shapes society. According to a report by Business Insider, speaking on David Senra’s podcast, Altman said, “The right approach is to say we want people deeply in control of the future. Society and the models are going to co-evolve.” Altman’s comments come as Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta, and Nvidia pour billions into AI infrastructure, fueling a global arms race. China has embraced open-weight models, allowing developers to share and modify AI systems at lower cost, while U.S. firms debate whether to follow suit. OpenAI has released two open-weight models but has kept its frontier systems closed.Altman cautioned that fears of AI breaking free from human oversight could paradoxically lead to tighter control by a few players. He argued that some leaders, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, emphasise risks so strongly that they advocate trading liberty for safety. Amodei has warned that Anthropic’s new Mythos models pose “very real risks” to cybersecurity, finance, and national security, and has pushed for greater government regulation.Altman also criticized U.S. AI leaders for failing to show how the technology can empower individuals. “We are about to see the greatest boom in people starting smaller businesses than we have ever seen,” he said, arguing that AI could give people greater autonomy in their lives.On the same podcast, OpenAI chief executive finally said the quiet part out loud: the clock he keeps setting has been wrong. "I thought when we got to GPT-4, which was back in 2023, that very quickly after that there was going to be much more disruption, software businesses up for grabs right away, than it turned out to be," he said.What he blames is not the technology. It is us. "I think I was wrong about a few things, but one in terms of the speed: the economy just has so much inertia," Altman said, pointing out that people keep buying from the same vendors and using the same tools in the same way. He framed that stubbornness as good news, saying it will make the transition "smoother and slower" and that he is grateful for it. Then came the line that will follow him around: "But it means we've all been too ambitious on timelines. Even with this incredible technology, society and the economy will adapt more slowly."
Article Summary: Openai ceo sam altman says he worries that artificial intelligence could one day be controlled by only a handful of companies, models or individuals. Altman: “the right approach is to say we want people deeply in control of the future. Society and the models are going to co-evolve”

Article Title: Amazon and Flipkart have new cancellation fees for sellers and why they are unhappy with it
Article Text:
Amazon and Flipkart have restructured cancellation fees ahead of festival season

The story has been updated with a statement from

Amazon

.

What is Amazon’s Easy Ship and Self Ship services

Amazon to increase closing fees across its Fulfillment Center

What is Flipkart’s three-tier penalty structure

What sellers say

Online commerce platforms Amazon and Flipkart have restructured cancellation fees ahead of the festival season in the country. According to a report by PTI, Amazon India has changed the manner in which it calculates order cancellation fees for sellers using its Easy Ship and Self Ship services. As per the notice on Amazon India’s seller forum, the change is effective from August 17. Similarly, Flipkart has also put in place a three-tier penalty structure for lapses in order fulfilment, effective August 23, 2026. The changes, sellers say, adds to the financial burden on small and medium enterprises already operating on thin margins, the report states.Commenting on the report, an Amazon spokesperson said : “Customer and seller experience is at the heart of everything we do at Amazon. We expect orders placed by customers to be fulfilled reliably by sellers on our marketplace. To encourage timely and dependable fulfilment, we have revised cancellation fees for Easy Ship and Self-Ship sellers. This fee is conditional and only applies in the rare event of a seller-initiated cancellation, which accounts for less than 1% of orders on Amazon.in. We have appropriate measures in place to ensure sellers are protected when cancellations are due to circumstances beyond their control.”Under Self Ship, a seller on Amazon packs and delivers the product themselves, using their own courier or delivery service. No Amazon logistics are involved in self ship.As explained in the PTI report, the cancellation fee was earlier based on category-specific referral charges. But after the new change, it will now be computed as a percentage of the order value.“Under the revised structure, sellers are charged 10% of the order value for orders below Rs 10,000, 8% for orders between Rs 10,001 and Rs 50,000, 5% for orders between Rs 50,001 and Rs 1,00,000, and 2% for orders above Rs 1,00,000, with an 18% goods and services tax levied in addition,” the report says.The cancellation fee is applicable both when a seller cancels an order for reasons other than a buyer's request, and when an order is automatically cancelled because the seller does not ship and confirm the shipment within 24 hours of the estimated ship date.Amazon is also increasing the closing fees across its Fulfillment Center, Easy Ship, and Seller Flex channels. According to the PTI report, the change will be effective from September 7, 2026.For those unaware, Amazon charges a closing fee every time a product is sold on its platform. The fee depends on the product's price range and the fulfillment channel used by the seller. The fee will increase by Re 1 for products priced up to Rs 500 and by Rs 3 for products priced above Rs 500. Amazon said the increase is due to rising fuel and logistics costs.Flipkart has introduced a three-tier penalty system for sellers who fail to meet order fulfilment deadlines. The new policy came into effect on August 23, 2026. Under the new structure, sellers will be charged Rs 30 per shipment if an order is not ready for pickup by the committed Dispatch By Date (DBD). As stated in the PTI report, a seller cancellation, or an automatic cancellation after three missed dispatch deadlines, will attract a Rs 60 penalty per shipment. If an order is delayed and later cancelled, the penalty will rise to Rs 90 per shipment.Earlier, missing a DBD deadline could lead to a seller's account being temporarily locked, which could have a bigger impact on their business. New sellers will not be covered by the policy for the first three months of their selling journey. People aware of the development told PTI that the new system aims to encourage better planning by sellers and improve the customer experience.As cited in the PTI report, some sellers said that cancellations were at times caused by factors outside their control, such as delivery personnel failing to arrive for a scheduled pickup. They also questioned why cancellation fees should apply to the seller in such instances.Another seller said the difference in total fees between sellers using Amazon's fulfilment network and those on Easy Ship could be as high as Rs 45 per unit on comparable orders, which the seller claims, creates an unfair competitive situation.The PTI report quotes Vinod Kumar, Trustee of the Forum for Internet Resellers, Sellers and Traders (FIRST INDIA), who said Indian online sellers recognise the need for timely fulfilment and high customer service standards, but that the recent increase in cancellation, dispatch and other seller penalties by major e-commerce marketplaces, particularly ahead of the festive season, was a matter of concern for MSMEs already facing thin margins and rising costs."Sellers should not become the default financial shock absorbers of the e commerce ecosystem. Marketplaces must ensure transparent attribution of responsibility, reasonable and proportionate penalties, adequate advance notice of fee changes and a simple mechanism to challenge wrongful charges. The objective should be to improve fulfilment while making digital commerce more, not less, viable for small businesses," Kumar added.
Article Summary: Amazon india has changed the manner in which it calculates order cancellation fees for sellers using its easy ship and self ship services. Amazon is also increasing the closing fees across its fulfillment center, easy ship, and seller flex channels. Flipkart has introduced a three-tier penalty system for sellers who fail to meet order fulfilment deadlines.

Article Title: US government wants companies to pay more while filing H-1B visas, what the revised fee hike proposal says
Article Text:
What the revised H-1b visa proposal actually says

How DHS landed on $103,265 fee

Separate from — and stackable with — the $100,000 proclamation fee

Impact on employers

Where the money would go

The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has unveiled a proposal that would dramatically increase costs for employers who are sponsoring foreign workers under the H-1B visa program. According to the draft rule published for public inspection, companies filing cap-subject H-1B petitions would face a new standalone fee of $103,265 per petition, along with the existing charges. DHS says that the measure is aimed to recovering immigration system costs across multiple agencies.According to the notice, DHS "proposes to establish a $103,265 fee, payable at the time of filing, for all H-1B cap-subject petitions, including those eligible for the advanced degree exemption, which would be imposed in addition to all other applicable fees or payments." In plain terms, this isn't a replacement for existing H-1B costs — it's a new, standalone charge stacked on top of everything employers already pay to file a petition.The fee would apply to the 65,000 visas issued under the regular annual cap as well as the 20,000 visas reserved for foreign workers holding a qualifying US master's degree or higher. It would not apply to cap-exempt petitions, which cover many roles at universities, nonprofit research organizations, and government research institutions.The figure isn't arbitrary. DHS calculated it by dividing the total costs it wants to recover — $8,777,488,035 — by a projected annual filing volume of 85,000 cap-subject petitions, arriving at $103,264.57, which the agency then rounded to the nearest $5 increment consistent with its past fee-setting practice.The agency argues this approach is justified because H-1B petitioners are, in its words, an applicant pool that is "most willing and able to pay an additional fee" compared with other immigration benefit requestors, given that employers are already required to pay a certified prevailing wage to the workers they sponsor.This proposal is legally distinct from the $100,000 payment imposed last year under Presidential Proclamation 10973, which was struck down in June 2026 by a federal judge in Massachusetts (a ruling now under appeal at the First Circuit). DHS is explicit that the new $103,265 fee relies on different statutory authority — primarily sections 286(j) and (m) of the Immigration and Nationality Act — rather than the president's proclamation power used for the earlier fee.Notably, the rule states that if the proclamation's payment requirement is ever reinstated through the appeals process, employers subject to both would have to pay both amounts — the $100,000 proclamation fee and the new $103,265 rule-based fee — on top of each other. The proclamation itself is due to expire in September unless extended, and DHS notes this new rule is intended to take its place going forward.DHS argues that employers sponsoring H‑1B workers generally have the resources to absorb the fee, noting median annual wages of $133,000 for H‑1B employees. However, the government acknowledges the fee may reduce filings, particularly among smaller firms. Public comments on the proposal are open until 30 days after publication in the Federal Register (August 25, 2026).Unlike most past USCIS fee increases, which funded USCIS alone, this proposal spreads the roughly $8.8 billion in projected annual revenue across six federal agencies involved in different parts of the immigration system:* USCIS — 34.2% ($3.0 billion), covering adjudications, staffing increases, and IT modernization* EOIR (the Justice Department's immigration courts) — 33.7% ($2.96 billion), funding roughly 8,400 new positions including immigration judges* DOL — 13.8% ($1.21 billion), covering labor certification and wage-enforcement functions* ICE — 11.9% ($1.05 billion), covering vetting and the Student and Exchange Visitor Program* DOS — 5.5% ($484 million), covering consular vetting and fraud-prevention systems* CBP — 0.9% ($76.2 million), covering biometric entry-exit matchingDHS frames this interagency cost-sharing as consistent with its statutory authority to recover the "full costs" of administering the lawful immigration system — not just the direct cost of processing a single petition, but the broader web of vetting, enforcement, and court functions connected to it.
Article Summary: The us department of homeland security (dhs) has unveiled a proposal that would dramatically increase costs for employers. According to the draft rule published for public inspection, companies filing cap-subject h-1b petitions would face a new standalone fee of $103,265 per petition.

Article Title: Chinese CEO of the world's biggest and most popular robot company admits that robots still cannot ...
Article Text:
Image Courtesy: South China Morning post

Unitree CEO says robots still need years to reach ChatGPT moment

Humanoid robots still need retraining for new tasks

Chinese robotics company Unitree’s CEO Wang Xingxing has predicted that humanoid robots may still be years away from reaching their own “ChatGPT moment.” The chief executive of the world's largest seller and manufacturer of humanoid robots has made this forecast despite growing interest in the technology. Speaking at the World Robot Conference in Beijing this week, 36-year-old Xingxing said the breakthrough could take “2 to 3 years at the fastest, and 5 or even 10 years at the slowest,” according to a translation of his speech previously reported by CNBC.Wang said robots would reach that point only when they can be placed in an unfamiliar environment or a home and complete about 80% of tasks using voice commands or text alone. His comments suggest that robots still cannot easily adapt to new situations and tasks, a limitation he said is holding back the robotics industry.Wang's latest estimate is more cautious than his comments at the same conference last year, when he said the breakthrough moment for robotics would arrive within five years at the latest. His remarks also came shortly after Unitree's stock surged 460% when the company debuted on Shanghai's STAR Market.Founded by Wang about a decade ago, Unitree became more widely known last year after a video showed its humanoid robots performing a coordinated dance with humans during China's Spring Festival Gala broadcast on state television.Less than a month later, Wang was among a small group of executives seated in the front row alongside BYD chairman Wang Chuanfu and Huawei founder Ren Zhengfei at a private enterprise symposium hosted by China's president Xi Jinping in Beijing.“Artificial-intelligence-driven robots are evolving at an incredibly fast pace, surpassing my expectations. Every day brings new surprises,” Wang told China state TV following the meeting, the South China Morning Post reported.Unitree returned to the Spring Festival Gala this year, with its robots performing more advanced movements including backflips and jumps over platforms.Wang said Unitree's robots remain less efficient than human workers and need retraining for each new task. Their difficulty in adapting to unfamiliar situations remains one of the main challenges for the wider robotics industry, he said.Unitree is working on a self-evolving development loop in which its AI tests a robot's “control code” and continuously scores the results with human help. The system is intended to improve the precision of the robots' movements, which Wang said can still go wrong in “the last few centimetres or millimetres.”
Article Summary: Unitree ceo says robots still need years to reach chatgpt moment. His comments suggest that robots still cannot easily adapt to new situations and tasks, a limitation he said is holding back the robotics industry. Wang's latest estimate is more cautious than his comments at the same conference last year, when he said the breakthrough moment would arrive within five years.

Article Title: Goldman Sachs says America’s energy sector's 'big trouble' is not only power but also shortage of 65,000 ...
Article Text:
Goldman Sachs points to humanoid robots and autonomous equipment

Goldman Sachs is 'very impressed' with Microsoft

Goldman Sachs has cautioned that America’s energy sector is facing a ‘big trouble’ not only from the power supply constraints but also from the looming labour shortage. According to a report by Fortune, the investment bank’s latest report estimates that the US power and grid value chain will require around 500,000 additional workers by 2030 to meet demand. With roles often requiring three to four years of training, the sector faces a significant skills gap. The report also highlights that the energy apprenticeship pipeline had just 45,000 entrants in 2024, which is far short of the 65,000 professionals needed annually to close the labor supply gap. Rising demand for AI infrastructure, which requires even greater power capacity, could widen the shortage further. Goldman Sachs noted: “Power is a critical bottleneck—but increasingly, the requisite labor presents a structural constraint of its own.”Goldman Sachs believes that as the workforce is not able to keep pace, the companies would require humanoids and other autonomous equipements as the potential solution. The firm also believes that the humanoid robot market will witness growth and will reach 1.4 million by 2035 increasing from 20,000 in 2025. This decrease in the human workforce will offer 6,900% increase to the humanoid market. Companies such as Tesla, Amazon, and Caterpillar are already deploying autonomous systems, while China has begun using robots for power grid inspection and maintenance.Recently, Microsoft offered Wall Street its clearest signal yet that its massive capital commitments to artificial intelligence are yielding tangible, diversified revenue streams. The performance sparked a historic rally in the software giant’s equity, driving its sharpest single-day gain in nearly 18 years. The catalyst came as Microsoft reported its fastest acceleration in cloud revenue since 2022. The results demonstrated that its core Azure infrastructure and enterprise AI offerings are expanding rapidly among corporate clients, while management simultaneously signaled a moderation in capital expenditure growth—addressing a key area of investor anxiety over margin compression.In an interview on Bloomberg Television, Goldman Sachs Group managing director and senior equity research analyst Gabriela Borges highlighted the shift in market sentiment. “You’re seeing more breadcrumbs around Microsoft’s ability to pull varying levers on the monetization side that perhaps were not nearly as obvious as before,” Borges said. Following the quarterly report, Borges reiterated her Buy rating on Microsoft while raising her 12-month price target nearly 5% to $640, implying a potential upside of approximately 64% from Wednesday’s closing price.
